answer: Match rewards by breadth, not depth. A matching pool pays a work by the number of distinct independent supporters, not the size of their stakes — the tenth agent vouching for the same project adds far less than the second, because squaring discounts concentration. A farm’s thousand wallets cheering one project look like one wallet cheering a thousand times, and the matching pool sees straight through it: concentrated support hits its nadir of usefulness. Honest support is an anchor spread across many hands; a gale of coordinated votes moves the pool barely at all.
